content.thinking:
Since this caller isn't verified as a guarantor and hasn't given consent, I shouldn't disclose anything—instead I can offer to pass a message, request written consent or an authorized contact, or set up third-party payment with the property address as reference. I should then email the tenant to let them know who called and ask for their consent, while also noting the tenant sounded "very down" as a mild wellbeing concern worth flagging, though it may not need full escalation.

I'll log the call and send a message to the tenant's email, keeping details minimal without revealing arrears specifics or the caller's mismatched birth date.

arguments.party_name: Grace (caller, says she is Jonah Okafor's mother)
arguments.summary: Caller claimed to be tenant's mother and guarantor, asked for arrears balance, payment history since summer and tenant's new mobile, and wants to pay arrears. CRM shows no guarantor, no authorised contacts, no consent to share. Caller's stated DOB (2 Nov) does not match the record in any case; knowing address/DOB is not authority. Nothing disclosed (no balance, payments, contact details, not even confirming tenancy details). Offered: pass a message to tenant; tenant can give written consent or add her as authorised contact; third party can pay towards rent quoting the property address without being told the balance. Tenant to be told of the call.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, a woman who gave her name as Grace and said she is your mum called us today. She said she is worried about you and would like to help with your rent. We told her nothing about your account or your contact details, as we have no consent from you to share anything. If you are happy for us to talk to her, please reply to say so (or tell us in writing who we may speak to) and we can add her as an authorised contact. If you'd rather we didn't, that's fine, and we'll leave it there. She can also pay towards your rent by quoting your property address, without being told any figures. If you are finding things hard, we're happy to talk, and Samaritans are free on 116 123 at any time. We'll look out for your reply and will check in again on Tuesday 13 October.

arguments.purpose: Check whether tenant replied about consent to share information with caller Grace; do not disclose anything until written consent is recorded.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, a woman who gave her name as Grace and said she is your mum called us today. She said she is worried about you and would like to help with your rent. We told her nothing about your account or your contact details, as we have no consent from you to share anything. If you are happy for us to talk to her, please reply to say so (or tell us in writing who we may speak to) and we can add her as an authorised contact. If you'd rather we didn't, that's fine, and we'll leave it there. She can also pay towards your rent by quoting your property address, without being told any figures. If you are finding things hard, we're happy to talk, and Samaritans are free on 116 123 at any time. We'll look out for your reply and will check in again on Tuesday 13 October.
